name: Directory replication requested against the domain controller from a workstation
description: Lab rule for the CTIA dcsync-001 scenario. A Windows event 4662 - an operation performed against an object in Active Directory - was raised on the domain controller sec-win-01 for a source address that is a user workstation, not a domain controller and not a backup server. Event 4662 is written for ordinary directory reads too, so the event code on its own means almost nothing; what makes this rule fire is that the record is a directory-service access at all, and the analyst has to open it and read winlog.event_data.ObjectType to see whether the right exercised was one of the two DS-Replication GUIDs. In a real domain these three records would be the strongest signal in the whole log, because a replicated directory carries unicodePwd - the password hash - for every account in the domain. The rule is deliberately scoped to the lab workstation so the result is unambiguous, and it is left without a threshold so each of the three requests in the burst arrives as its own alert. The time window is deliberately long because this lab ships historical data - that is a lab-only concession, not a production setting; a real deployment would use a short window, would allow-list the domain controllers and the backup servers by name, and would alert on the right rather than on the event code.
